title: Length pacing and pad evaporation engine for runtime bucketing
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Reduce wasted tokens and improve tail latency by introducing a runtime component that paces incoming requests by sequence-length cohorts, dynamically thins padding across micro-batches (pad evaporation), and emits kernel hints for attention and decoding paths. The component ("Length Pacer") sits in the prefill/packing stage and produces micro-batch shapes optimized for kernel selection and KV cache usage. It targets both prefill-heavy workloads (long context prompts) and mixed prefill/decode workloads common in chat assistants.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end synthetic benchmark shows >=18% average pad token reduction vs baseline conservative packer at 99th percentile latency target
No regression (>2%) in median token throughput for short-chat workloads after kernel hinting integration
Automated rollout (canary then 100%) via Console with observability panels: pad count, shaped batch sizes, kernel hints applied, and end-to-end latency delta
PRs merged for runtime and scheduler components with unit + integration tests and perf harness results attached to the PR
design_decisions: Prefer sequence-length cohorts sized by token-entropy buckets instead of fixed-size bins to adapt to heavy-tailed distributions
Emit kernel selection hints (e.g., low-memory-quantized vs fast-fp16) rather than hard routing to allow runtime to fallback on capacity constraints
Apply pad evaporation heuristics only when prefill-to-decode ratio > 0.7 to avoid harming short-turn chat latency
Use conservative latency SLO guardrails: if shaped micro-batch introduces >5% 99th latency increase for any tenant in canary, automatically revert to baseline packer
tradeoffs: More aggressive pad evaporation lowers cost but risks increased variance in GPU utilization and potential 99th percentile latency spikes
Emitting kernel hints increases scheduler complexity and coupling between packer and kernel selector, but reduces repeated profiling overhead
Cohort sizing heuristic introduces extra per-request compute in prefill stage; offset by reduced token work on attention kernels
Conservative canary strategy increases rollout time for wins but reduces risk of customer-visible regressions
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Spike completed comparing entropy-bucket cohorting vs quantile bucketing on 10M request sample. Entropy bucket reduced pad tokens by ~22% at P95 on aggregator workload
2026-02-25: Prototyped Length Pacer as a separate scheduler pass; emits shaped batch descriptors and kernel_hint tags. Initial microbench shows 12% pad reduction with no median latency regression
2026-03-03: Integrated kernel_hint plumbing into runtime kernel selector API; added compatibility layer for older runtime nodes without hints

2026-03-08: Canary run started in us-west with 5% traffic for internal dev tenants. Observability panel added to Console (links below). Early signals: pad reduction ~15%, slight 99th latency drift (+1.6%) on one tenant with very bursty traffic
2026-03-10: Pulled canary from that tenant, adjusted cohort sizing (increase min cohort size) and retesting. Preparing PR for runtime changes and perf report
qa_plan: Unit tests for cohorting algorithm and pad accounting
Integration test with runtime kernel selector fallback paths mocked
Perf harness runs across three representative workloads: assistant-chat (short-turn), long-context summarization, and mixed low-latency conversational
Canary rollout with automatic revert configured and a 48-hour observation window
rollout_notes: Start with internal dev orgs only, 5% traffic for 24h
If pad reduction >10% and 99th latency delta <2% continue to 25% for 48h
Monitor token-cost curve and per-tenant 99th percentile latency; if any tenant shows >2.5% regression revert immediately
Expose per-tenant override flag in Console to opt-out until stable
